analysis: Examined units cover CI-only test files for the threat-review tooling: .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py and test-threat-budget.py. The head of test-threat-bedrock.py adds workload call-policy tests (lines 302-378). These cover planned-call admission, the 500-call emergency ceiling, 16384 max output tokens, invalid policy rejection, and read timeouts of 240/600s with no SDK retries. Lines 431-498 add large-scan hierarchical integration tests. Lines 539-557 add final-incomplete handoff tests asserting human review and that clean() is false. In test-threat-budget.py, head lines 949-982 add three tests. One covers the manual rerun hand-off (MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED, no paid calls, run id 123-2, not clean). One bounds runtime_seconds to 60-3000. One checks the workload-limit diagnostic at the integration planning stage. These changes are tests only. They do not touch the provider, coordinator, native runtime, keys, attestation, or the authorization assets/boundaries in the threat model (A-001..A-017, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011). The tests assert fail-closed merge-gate behavior: unknown usage stops spending, there is no fallback on ambiguous failures, stale or other-attempt results cannot clear, and membership is rechecked. They also assert that private content is excluded from the usage ledger. The implementations under test (threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_scan.py, merge_policy.py, threat-review-gate.py, threat-model-review.py) are not in these units. Their actual enforcement of these contracts is therefore unverified here and should be checked in the batches containing those files. Raising the call/runtime ceilings (500 calls, 3000s) is a CI cost/availability matter outside the provider threat model's scope. No product security regression was identified.
